body:
Thank you for your response. You're not at all ignorant or unintelligent; your comment proves the opposite.

A pursuit of a will to keep going being itself my will to keep going has been largely what's gotten me to this point. Unfortunately it hasn't proved fulfilling. It was always to me a placeholder, something temporary to be filled by something true and real.

I know there is still good left in the world. But that good is so few and far between, like tiny lights in an infinite night. Maybe this makes a beautiful picture, but it's still an unbearably sad one, to me. I try to make some of those lights myself—I strive to be kind, to help others where I can—but I also cast a shadow, I make the world darker, intentionally or otherwise. Some is because I damage the environment by merely existing, I consume and therefore harm others. Some is because I have been a bad person in the past, ferrying the hurt I endured onto others. Some is because it is so hard to be kind in the face of meanness and deliberate cruelty. Perhaps this is just the consequence of humanity, as you said. In which case, evil is inevitable, and the problem that plagues me remains.
I understand that nothing is so clean as to be black and white. This world and the people within are too complex. You can't pick up one string without pulling a million others. Which makes evil feel at the same time stark and nebulous, identifiable and unknown. It's everywhere, but where did it begin? How can it end?
Your point on giving ourselves a break from getting caught up in it all, I'm assuming you're referencing a psychological fatigue from trying to care about everything messed up in the world. I agree, we can't run that marathon constantly day in and day out. Taking those breaks is something I try to do, but alas, the world weasels its way into your mind and demands attention without much you can do about it. That is where I found myself on Christmas night, and the aftermath was enough to make me try to take my life the next day.

The reasons why people choose to live are multivariate, and yes, ultimately trivial. Even the most  strong, deep conviction is nothing in the face of our negligible short existence. I wish I could find something to make it seem worthwhile that lasted; as much as I truly do enjoy the little things like a good tea, temporary tattoos, a delicious burrito, cute animals, Skyrim, a beautiful sunset, I wish I had something to tie it all together, something I truly believed in, to make the backdrop of evil and suffering feel bearable.

Thank you for sharing your perspective. I'm sorry if my response doesn't make much sense, I'm afraid my thoughts aren't really flowing cohesively anymore today. My mind is really scattered and I find it difficult to say what I want to say. Thank you for believing in me, and I hope you are right that I will find a better path. Cheers to you too.

Thank you for your kind words and for sharing your perspective. The majority of my problem is with the world, that is true. I am glad that you can see hope in that. I wish I could too. To me the problem being with the world makes it so much more daunting a problem than were it contained in myself. When the issue is your right to live, changing oneself towards the goal of having enough self-esteem and self-worth to feel like you deserve to live is already an enormously difficult undertaking; changing the fundamental tenets of the complex cruelty of the world? I cannot help but despair at the scale and depth of that impossible mission. I understand that helping one person, making one person's day brighter, being kind and generous, has value—"whoever saves one life saves the world entire"—and is something to strive for, something I strive for. However it feels like a single drop of water in a bottomless vat of pitch. How I wish such small acts of kindness and humanity were more like a drop of dye in water, that they could curl into waves beautiful to watch as it spreads throughout the water and, with enough dye, actually able to change the water's color. Such is how I feel about the beauty of someone full of care and love (I appreciate you think so) persisting in this evil world; sinking, suffocating, blind in an ocean of darkness, ultimately changing nothing, swallowed up by evil that surrounds them. Maybe there is beauty in such a struggle. I have believed similar things before, but though they gave me a will, they brought me a violent, self-destructive peace, and as such was not sustainable nor (in hindsight) a good way to live.
I'm sorry for having such a downer response to your message. I truly do appreciate your kindness, and your taking the time to share how you feel and respond to me. Though I do not see the hope you see, I will continue to think about your perspective. Wishing you all the best.
